transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name], and I'll be speaking with you today. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in to see me?

I guess… it’s rats. Just the thought I might see one at work has gotten bad. I clean buildings, and now I can’t do some areas, like trash rooms or old parts of the building, even though I know it’s probably not really dangerous.
Is your fear of rats limited to places like trash rooms and old parts of buildings, or does it also happen in other places where you might see them, like outside or in your home?

Mostly it’s at work… like trash rooms or those older areas. The thought I might see one there is enough that I just can’t do parts of my cleaning anymore, even though I know it’s probably not really dangerous.
Have you ever avoided other places, like public parks or alleys, because you were afraid you might see a rat there?

Yeah… sometimes. I’ll avoid going by alley dumpsters if I can. At work I also try to skip routes with basements, storage rooms, or laundry areas. If I have to go in, I leave the door open and just hurry through it.
Are there other situations or things besides rats that make you feel anxious or avoidant, such as being in open spaces, being in crowded places, or being around people?
Not really… I mean, I don’t think so. It’s mostly the rat thing. Crowds or people don’t bother me like that.
How long have you felt this way about rats, and has it caused you any significant distress or problems in your daily life outside of avoiding certain areas at work or in public?
About two years, I guess. It started after I moved into this older apartment building… people there were always talking about rats, and since then it’s just kind of stuck with me.
When you think about rats or encounter places where they might be, do you ever feel sudden, intense physical reactions like a racing heart, sweating, or shortness of breath?
Yeah… it happens fast. If I hear scratching in a wall or see something move near a pipe, my heart starts pounding and my hands shake. I just feel like I need to get out right then.
